stories.title: Van Buren Township Planning Commission approves data center plan
stories.summary: The Van Buren Township Planning Commission approved the final site plan for the Project Cannoli Data Center, developed by Panattoni for Google, despite resident opposition. stories.title: EMU Board of Regents passes contract agreements with teacher and police unions
stories.summary: The Eastern Michigan University Board of Regents approved new three-year contracts with its teacher and police unions, including salary increases, healthcare adjustments, and an AI policy for faculty work and research to protect intellectual property. These agreements aim to support employees in serving students.

stories.title: Samuel and Dan Habib speak about producing and directing ‘The Ride Ahead’
stories.summary: Filmmakers Samuel and Dan Habib discuss their documentary "The Ride Ahead," which explores Samuel's transition to adulthood with a disability. The film, co-directed by the father-son duo, emphasizes authentic representation and features interviews with disability advocates. Dan Habib is a University of Michigan alum, and the film will screen at the Marsal Family School of Education.

stories.title: Many older adults make Medicare decisions quickly, most don’t change plans
stories.summary: A University of Michigan survey indicates that 60% of older adults spend less than an hour choosing Medicare coverage, with 80% retaining their previous year's plan. This suggests many may miss options better suited to their needs, especially given changes in available plans and drug cost policies for 2027.

inputFacts.title: Many older adults make Medicare decisions quickly, most don’t change plans
inputFacts.summary: A University of Michigan survey shows 60% of older adults spend less than an hour choosing Medicare coverage during Open Enrollment, with 80% sticking to their previous year's plans. Researchers emphasize the need for more thorough review of options, as many may not be aware of changes affecting costs and coverage. The 2027 Open Enrollment period runs from October 15 to December 7.

stories.title: Massive Google data center faces decision day in Michigan’s Van Buren Township
stories.summary: Van Buren Township is poised to approve a Google data center, with officials negotiating agreements to mitigate potential environmental impacts and utility cost increases for residents. The township supervisor indicated that Google will cover any residential water rate hikes and has reduced generator reliance, while tax incentives were used to secure advanced environmental controls and sound dampening measures.

inputFacts.title: Massive Google data center faces decision day in Michigan’s Van Buren Township
inputFacts.summary: The Van Buren Township Planning Commission is set to vote on the final site for a Google data center on October 14. Residents express concerns about environmental impact and utility costs, while Supervisor Kevin McNamara emphasizes the need to comply with zoning laws and negotiate community benefits. The township has secured agreements to mitigate potential issues like water rate increases and power outages.

inputFacts.title: Great Lakes Crossing, Twelve Oaks Mall getting new stores, attractions
inputFacts.summary: Twelve Oaks Mall and Great Lakes Crossing are adding new stores and attractions in 2026, including Popmart, Platform, Body and Soul Medical Spa, and Round1 Bowling and Arcade. Simon Property Group emphasizes enhancing in-person shopping experiences with mixed-use offerings. Great Lakes Crossing will host a trick-or-treat event on October 17, with more store openings planned.

inputFacts.title: Are you too old to rake leaves? Why it may be better to leave them
inputFacts.summary: Experts warn that raking leaves can pose significant health risks, particularly for older adults or those with heart disease, as the activity can strain the heart similarly to shoveling snow. Medical professionals advise starting slowly and avoiding overexertion, while environmental experts suggest leaving leaves to decompose naturally for ecological benefits. Southern Illinois University and the Cleveland Clinic highlight the risks of sudden physical exertion after periods of inactivity.

inputFacts.title: Michigan roadside parks are closing. When gates lock for winter
inputFacts.summary: Most Michigan roadside parks will close on Oct. 29 as the Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT) prepares for winter. Nearly all 82 parks maintained by MDOT close each fall in late October and reopen in late April. Rest areas along major freeways and roads remain open 24/7 for travelers.

inputFacts.title: Disgraced Michigan doctor Farid Fata seeks early release again -- here's what victims say
inputFacts.summary: Disgraced former Michigan oncologist Farid Fata is seeking compassionate release from his 45-year federal sentence, but survivors and families oppose his release, citing lasting physical harm. Fata pleaded guilty in 2014 to unnecessary cancer treatments, and his prior compassionate-release request was denied in March 2025. Victims may submit statements to U.S. District Judge Jonathan Grey by October 23, 2026.

inputFacts.title: Grand Valley's corpse flower blooms. How to see, smell it now
inputFacts.summary: Grand Valley State University's corpse flower is in full bloom, with extended greenhouse hours for visitors. The plant, which smells like rotting flesh, last bloomed in 2024 and is now following an unexpected prolific blooming pattern. Greenhouse hours have been expanded through October 18 to accommodate visitors.

inputFacts.title: 'Shoot every person in there': Man accused of threatening crowd at Holly restaurant reopening
inputFacts.summary: Daniel James Gibson, 26, was charged with making a false report or threat of terrorism after allegedly threatening to shoot people at Andy’s Place’s Oct. 10 reopening celebration in Holly. Police reported Gibson attempted to bring alcohol to the event, climbed a fence after being removed, and threatened attendees while reaching into his backpack. He was arrested near Crapo Park with alcohol and a large knife, though no gun was found.

inputFacts.title: State regulators approve nearly $140M rate hike for Consumers Energy natural gas customers
inputFacts.summary: State regulators approved a $139.2 million annual natural gas rate increase for Consumers Energy, reducing the utility's original $240 million request by 42%. The 4.3% rate increase will take effect on Nov. 1, adding approximately $4 per month to customer bills. Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel urged regulators to cut the request by more than half, citing concerns about inflated costs and unreasonable profit margins.

inputFacts.title: Detroit health fair brings free screenings, groceries, resources to families
inputFacts.summary: A coalition of local groups including New Beginnings Community Development Corporation, Sound Mind Sound Body, and the Unify Detroit Coalition organized a free health fair to address common barriers like cost, time, and transportation. Project director Junious Williams explained how the organizers aimed to eliminate these excuses by providing accessible services and resources.

inputFacts.title: Google wins zoning approval for huge data center near Detroit airport
inputFacts.summary: Google's proposed 282-acre hyperscale data center (Project Cannoli) near Detroit Metro Airport received final zoning approval from Van Buren Township's Planning Commission despite resident opposition. The project, which will bring significant investment and tax revenue to the area, faces concerns about noise pollution, construction impacts, and environmental effects. Local officials and developers highlight the economic benefits, while residents and activists continue to push back against the development.

inputFacts.title: East Jackson School Board president challenges incumbent rep in 46th District
inputFacts.summary: Democrat Jan Maino, East Jackson School Board president, is challenging two-term Republican state Rep. Kathy Schmaltz in Michigan’s reliably red 46th House District. Both candidates focus on affordability and education, with Maino advocating for affordable housing projects and Medicaid preservation, while Schmaltz emphasizes tax cuts and per-pupil funding increases. The race is part of WEMU's 2026 midterm election coverage.
